title: PowPrediCT: Cross-Stage Power Prediction with Circuit-Transformation-Aware Learning
problem: Modeling circuit power at the placement stage is challenging because the clock tree and final signal routing are unavailable. Additionally, circuit transformations such as restructuring and gate sizing can invalidate power predictions derived from earlier design stages.
motivation: Accurate power prediction at early VLSI design stages is critical for effective power optimization and enabling informed design decisions.
method: The model predicts power consumption at the placement stage (when component positions are assigned). It has a dedicated model for the clock tree (the network distributing timing signals throughout the chip). To handle circuits that change during optimization—like restructuring connections or gate sizing—it learns power patterns from training data and adapts based on physical layout and how components connect.
key_novelty: This is the first power prediction model at the placement stage that stays accurate when circuits are modified during optimization (such as restructuring or gate sizing).
contributions: First circuit-transformation-aware power prediction model at VLSI placement stage
Dedicated clock tree modeling for early-stage power analysis without complete routing information
Train-and-calibrate scheme integrating topological and layout features
Significant reduction in cross-stage power analysis error compared to Innovus

metrics.accuracy: reduced cross-stage power analysis error vs Innovus

primary_theme: early-stage power prediction in VLSI placement
